account:
Today I have kept my usual appointments, but the unusual business is a large, deliberately unexplained gathering in the town hall at eighteen. I saw builder and innkeeper putting bread into a hall table chest yesterday, and the hall has lanterns. Neighbour says all two hundred fresh loaves were verified there this morning and guests need bring nothing. She has been spreading the innkeeper's invitation. Builder personally invited me, asking that I indulge them in keeping the occasion's details until eighteen. Innkeeper described it to the secretary as community hospitality, with the programme announced at eighteen and no prepared remarks needed. He is to meet me at my office at seventeen-fifty and escort me there.

Builder, innkeeper and neighbour are clearly involved in the preparations; secretary is helping keep my appointments and coordinating the escort, though she has not claimed to know the occasion. My suspicion is that this is a friendly surprise celebration or community feast, possibly with some special attention intended for me. That last part is only a guess: nobody has told me what it celebrates. The secrecy seems intentional rather than evidence of wrongdoing.

There has been talk about a bridge or port change at the bakery, but I have no verified transport change. The baker reported buying eight hay bales, and the miller handles grain stocks; I still lack a full stock report. Those fragments do not establish another scheme. Official business has been quiet: no council letters or new correspondence have reached the secretary, and her latest check found only the three books in the office chest. For now I am waiting at the office for the promised escort rather than pressing people to spoil the surprise.
